name: Reaction Test
description: A lightweight content / comprehension reaction test (Nielsen Norman content testing, the 5-second test): React (fan) -> Synthesize (waist). Show a concrete artifact to a segment-diverse persona group and read how they react — fast, honest, two steps.
when_to_use: When you have something concrete and want a quick read of how your audience reacts — a blog post, headline, landing copy, a single screen or message: what lands, what confuses, and how the wording feels.

presentation.summary: Show a concrete artifact to your audience and get a fast, honest read on how it lands.
presentation.jobs: Quick gut-checks on wording, copy, messaging or a single screen before you ship it.

deck.purpose: Enable a ship, revise or review decision for one fixed stimulus.
deck.target_core_slides: 6–8 slides for a 10-minute stakeholder readout; roughly one decision beat per 60–90 seconds.
deck.story_shape: Orienting cover (tested artifact/journey + audience + test question) → decision dashboard → admitted stimulus → cohort lenses → reaction movement → editable proposed revision → release gate. Combine proof on the decision slide instead of spreading one finding over sparse slides.

story_beats.question: What should happen next, how strong is the signal, and why?
What exactly did the cohort see?
What concrete screen, copy or interaction should replace the current one?
What is kept, changed and validated next?

appendix: optional persona details only when decision-relevant
speaker_notes: what to say while the visual is on screen
transition to the next decision beat
avoid: a cover that starts with unexplained A/B verdict language before naming what was tested
headlines longer than 12 words or 68 characters
describing an available stimulus only in prose
separate recommendation prose when a proposed revision can be shown
more than five appendix slides by default
calling synthetic reactions observed customer behavior

steps.name: React
steps.intent: Show the concrete artifact (copy, headline, a screen, a message) to a segment-diverse persona group. Capture honest first impressions, what is understood versus confusing, what resonates or jars, and the emotional reaction. Keep it fast — no leading.

work_items.title: Reaction · first impression and comprehension
work_items.intent: Run a segment-diverse council on first impression, information scent, comprehension and concrete confusion points. Cite only the admitted stimulus and persona memory.

work_items.title: Reaction · trust, gaps and action readiness
work_items.intent: Run a distinct council angle on trust, missing information, comparison expectations and readiness to take the next action. Include skeptical and non-target voices.

steps.name: Synthesize
steps.intent: Converge: what landed, what confused, the wording and structure that helped or hurt, and concrete revision recommendations — ready to apply.
